assessment.nobel_worthiness: Methods for estimating demand with differentiated products and endogenous prices, plus dynamic industry models, turned empirical industrial organisation into a quantitative field. The tools are used in merger review, antitrust, auctions, health and trade. The impact is broad, methodological and policy-relevant.
assessment.attribution: The core demand-side framework (Berry 1994; Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes 1995) and the dynamic-oligopoly estimation line (Pakes with collaborators) make a coherent three-person core. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are important but can be left out under the three-laureate limit.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use, replication and extension. Many applications and a large body of derived methods leave little doubt about durability.
uncertainties: Choosing among Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin involves a judgement on credit that I cannot settle from the longlist alone.
Whether the committee would treat this as econometrics or industrial organisation, and how it compares with other methods candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Systematic formal and empirical analysis of how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. It created modern political economics as a field and is closely tied to long-run development. Its policy relevance for institutional design is large.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central pair (formal models, then empirical work on constitutions). Besley is an equally strong third through state capacity, accountability and the citizen-candidate model. Credit is fairly clear within this trio.
assessment.maturity: More than 30 years of work, with a long record of replication and extension, so timing is not an issue.
uncertainties: Disclosure: my profile lists a corruption paper co-authored with Persson and Rothstein, and my work is close to this literature. I rely on the common criteria and note the conflict without trying to resolve it.
The 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity may weigh on timing or thematic overlap.
The unit of recognition could be drawn differently (for example, without Besley).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-firm trade models changed how economists think about who exports, how trade reallocates resources within industries, and where the gains from trade come from. They also opened the way to firm-level empirics across countries.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman, with collaborators, extended the framework to FDI, the extensive margin and inequality. Redding is a significant contributor, but I rank his claim slightly lower.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of use. It has been confirmed in firm-level data and shows up in policy evaluation.
uncertainties: Melitz built on earlier work (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum; Krugman's earlier prize), so the boundary of credit is arguable.
Overlap with B015 and B039 in international trade.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model gave a tractable, widely used non-cooperative foundation for bargaining. It underlies work in labour, industrial organisation, political economy and macro. Rubinstein and Wolinsky's market-bargaining extension linked bargaining theory to decentralised trade.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is clearly primary. Wolinsky's contribution to markets with search and bargaining is distinct. Binmore's work is important, but I see it as less decisive for the core result.
assessment.maturity: More than 40 years of continuous use and extension. The results are established.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with game-theory prizes already awarded (Nash, Selten, Harsanyi, Myerson, Maskin and others).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A sufficient-statistics approach and credible empirical estimates of behavioural responses to taxation brought optimal-tax theory into contact with data. The work informs real tax design and policy debate on top rates, transfers and tax salience.
assessment.attribution: Saez's work on the elasticity of taxable income and optimal taxation, and Chetty's sufficient-statistics formulation and quasi-experimental evidence, are central. Slemrod and Stantcheva are important contributors whose claims I rank lower.
assessment.maturity: Substantial for Saez's work. Chetty's contributions are partly more recent, although the sufficient-statistics approach is already widely adopted.
uncertainties: Chetty also appears in B031 and Saez in B050, so the committee would need to decide how to separate overlapping bodies of work.
Some of the empirical elasticity estimates remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HANK models integrate household heterogeneity and incomplete markets with nominal rigidities. They change how monetary and fiscal policy transmission is understood, especially through the marginal propensity to consume and distributional channels. Central banks and ministries now use these models.
assessment.attribution: The Kaplan-Moll-Violante trio defines the framework, and a three-person limit fits it. Earlier heterogeneous-agent work (Aiyagari, Huggett, Krusell-Smith) is acknowledged but outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: The central papers date from about 2018. Policy adoption is rapid, but the long-run confirmation is less than for the older candidates.
uncertainties: It may be too early to judge lasting importance.
Precursor credit to earlier heterogeneous-agent macro is not covered by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A framework and empirical method for quantifying how misallocation of inputs across firms lowers aggregate productivity. It helps explain cross-country income differences, linking micro-data to macro development questions, with implications for policy.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) is the central paper. Restuccia and Rogerson's related work is important but outside the credited trio's core shared paper. Restuccia is credited here, but I give priority to Hsieh and Klenow.
assessment.maturity: More than 15 years of use. It is widely applied, though with continuing measurement debates.
uncertainties: Debate about measurement error and what the measured wedges represent.
Whether this stands as a distinct discovery or as an application of earlier growth and productivity work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the study of local labour-market effects of trade shocks changed the understanding of wage inequality, automation and globalisation. It has strong policy and public relevance and is broadly influential across labour, trade and macro.
assessment.attribution: The skill-biased-technical-change and task work (Autor and Katz) and the China-shock work (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) are somewhat distinct strands. A three-person selection needs a judgement. Other contributors, notably Acemoglu, are outside the list and already recognised in 2024.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades for the technology work and about a decade for the China-shock work. Evidence is largely confirmed, though some results remain debated.
uncertainties: Combining two strands under one prize may dilute the clarity of attribution.
Overlap with 2024 prize themes and with recent labour-economics recognition.
Some long-run interpretations of the China shock are contested.
